paras: The attempted lynching of Rufus Martin was an unsuccessful effort, reported from Fort Worth, Texas, to lynch a Black man accused of killing a farmer in early November 1903. Martin survived, and on November 10 a jury sentenced him to death, a verdict carried by wire to papers in Nebraska and Wyoming.

Martin, described as "a negro," was accused of waylaying and killing a farmer named Chas. Schwackhammer about a week before November 10. One printing of the dispatch said he also robbed the farmer, while another said he killed him "by stabbing him."

At some point between the killing and the trial, Martin "narrowly escaped lynching." The reports give no date, place or description of the attempt, and do not say who tried to lynch him or how he was saved.

Martin was tried in Fort Worth within about a week of the killing, and the jury returned a death verdict on the morning of November 10, 1903. No report of a sentence being carried out, an appeal, or any arrest of those who tried to lynch him was found.

The case is known only from a short Fort Worth dispatch dated November 10 that ran the same day in two papers far from Texas. The Beatrice Daily Express of Nebraska printed it as a special under the headline "Sentenced to Die," with the subhead "Negro Who Murdered a Farmer One Week Ago Is Convicted by a Jury Today." The Laramie Republican of Wyoming ran the same item as "Death Verdict Returned" among a column of Washington telegraph news.

Both versions stated the killing as fact rather than as a charge, and treated the near-lynching as a one-sentence afterthought to the verdict. No coverage in Texas papers or in the Black press was found.

The two printings differ in detail: the Beatrice paper said Martin robbed the farmer and spelled his name Schwackhammer, while the Laramie paper said he stabbed him and spelled the name Schwackhanmer, probably variants of one trimmed dispatch.

bases: Both reports say Martin, accused of killing a farmer, 'narrowly escaped' a lynching before his trial (A1, A2); the episode is an unsuccessful lynching attempt, with no details given.
A1 and A2 are two printings of the same Fort Worth dispatch of Nov. 10, with near-identical wording, so they are not independent reports (A1, A2).

accounts.label: Fort Worth wire dispatch
accounts.gist: A jury returned a death verdict against Martin, a Black man who had waylaid and killed a farmer a week earlier; he had narrowly escaped lynching.

framing.detail: The Beatrice Daily Express headed the item 'Sentenced to Die / Negro Who Murdered a Farmer', presenting the killing as fact and the near-lynching as an aside.
The Laramie Republican ran it as 'Death Verdict Returned' among Washington telegraph items, again stating the killing as fact.
